metaTitle: Basement Finishing Contractors in Ontario: A Guide
metaDescription: What Ontario homeowners should know before finishing a basement, including permits, egress windows, moisture control, costs and red flags to avoid.
intro: Finishing a basement adds livable space, but it comes with permit, moisture and egress requirements that are easy to overlook. A contractor who understands these details up front avoids costly rework later, especially in older homes where foundations and ceiling heights vary.
whatToLookFor: A building permit pulled before framing begins
Correct egress window sizing if any room will be used as a bedroom
A clear plan for vapour barrier and moisture management against foundation walls
Experience finishing basements in homes of a similar age
A proper insulation approach for below-grade walls, not just interior framing
typicalCostNotes: Basement finishing costs vary with square footage, ceiling height obstacles, whether a bathroom or suite kitchen is added, and how much moisture remediation the foundation needs first. A simple recreation room typically costs less than a legal secondary suite with its own egress, plumbing and fire separation requirements. Ask whether the quote already includes permit fees and any required foundation waterproofing work, since remediation found partway through can otherwise become a costly add-on.
questionsToAsk: Will this project need a permit, and are egress windows required?
How will you manage moisture and vapour barrier against the foundation?
Is there any sign of past water intrusion we should address first?
If this becomes a bedroom or suite, does the design meet code?
What insulation type and R-value are you using on basement walls?
redFlags: Suggesting you skip the permit to save time or money
No mention of moisture testing or a vapour barrier strategy
Framing over walls with visible past water staining without addressing it
